description: Rule catalog for the stable-build guard (scripts/guard.mjs). Rule ids are stable. Each evidence.quote is verbatim from evidence.url (compare after collapsing whitespace: the docs wrap lines). Detection logic lives in scripts/guard/rules.mjs; fixtures in test/guard/fixtures/<id>/.
suffix: advisory: the edit was applied; silence with `stable-build-ignore <id>`

rules.title: Native USDC value built with 6 decimals
rules.flags: A transaction `value` (sendTransaction, writeContract, ethers overrides) or Solidity `msg.value` / `{value: ...}` built with 6 decimals: parseUnits(x, 6), * 10n ** 6n, 1e6.
rules.message: Native value (tx `value`, `msg.value`) on Arc is USDC with 18 decimals; a 6-decimal amount moves 10^12 times less than intended.
rules.fix: Use parseUnits(x, 18) for native value, or send 6-decimal amounts with USDC.transfer on the ERC-20 interface (0x3600…0000).

evidence.quote: Native USDC uses 18 decimals (`eth_getBalance`, `address.balance`); the ERC-20 interface uses 6 decimals (`balanceOf`).

notes: EIP-3009 / permit typed-data messages (validAfter, validBefore, spender, deadline) use 6 decimals correctly and are not flagged.

The gas-and-fees page example sends `value: ethers.parseUnits("1", 6)` labelled "1 USDC via native send" (https://docs.arc.io/arc/references/gas-and-fees); that contradicts the 18-decimal native interface on the wallets and EVM-differences pages. This rule follows the latter.

rules.title: USDC ERC-20 amount built with 18 decimals
rules.flags: transfer / approve / transferFrom on USDC (0x3600… address, a usdc-named contract or ABI) with parseEther, parseUnits(x, 18), 10n ** 18n, 1e18 or `cast to-wei`.
rules.message: The USDC ERC-20 interface (transfer, approve, transferFrom) uses 6 decimals; an 18-decimal amount asks for 10^12 times more.
rules.fix: Use parseUnits(x, 6) for USDC ERC-20 calls; keep 18 decimals for native value only.

evidence.quote: Optional ERC-20 interface for interacting with the native USDC balance. Uses 6 decimals.

rules.title: Native and ERC-20 USDC balances added or shown twice
rules.flags: getBalance / eth_getBalance / address(x).balance / msg.value added to balanceOf, or UI labels for both a native and an ERC-20 USDC balance.
rules.message: Native USDC (getBalance, 18 decimals) and ERC-20 USDC (balanceOf, 6 decimals) are one balance; adding them or showing two rows double-counts.
rules.fix: Read one view (getBalance scaled by 18 decimals, or balanceOf by 6) and show a single USDC balance row.

two-rows.message: Native USDC and ERC-20 USDC are labelled as separate balances; they are the same balance.

evidence.quote: Don't display native USDC and ERC-20 USDC as separate balance rows: they're the same balance.

rules.title: maxFeePerGas or gasPrice below 20 gwei
rules.flags: A literal maxFeePerGas / gasPrice under 20 gwei: parseGwei, parseUnits(x, 'gwei'), bigint or hex wei, `--gas-price` / `--with-gas-price`, `gas_price` in TOML.
rules.message: maxFeePerGas/gasPrice under 20 gwei: the transaction never gets a receipt. Depending on the RPC it is rejected as `transaction underpriced` or silently dropped.
rules.fix: Set maxFeePerGas to at least 20 gwei; read current fees with eth_gasPrice or eth_feeHistory.

evidence.quote: Transactions with `maxFeePerGas` lower than 20 Gwei are silently dropped by the mempool.

notes: maxPriorityFeePerGas is not checked: the gas-and-fees page says a 0 Gwei tip is accepted.
The gas-and-fees table labels the 20 Gwei floor "Minimum base fee (testnet)"; the EVM-differences page states it with no network qualifier.

The outcome below the floor differs by page: evm-differences says such transactions "are silently dropped by the mempool. They produce no error receipt"; gas-and-fees lists the error `transaction underpriced` for maxFeePerGas below the 20 Gwei floor and says they "may remain pending indefinitely or fail outright" (https://docs.arc.io/arc/references/gas-and-fees, checked 2026-10-04). The message covers both.

rules.title: getLogs range over 10,000 blocks, or from a fixed start block to latest
rules.flags: getLogs / getContractEvents / queryFilter / eth_getLogs / cast logs from a fixed start block (0, earliest, a literal or UPPER_CASE const) to latest, or a range of more than 10,000 blocks, i.e. toBlock - fromBlock of 10,000 or more (latestBlock - 10000n to latest is 10,001 blocks; fromBlock 1_000_000n to toBlock 1_050_000n). Exactly 10,000 blocks (from + 10_000n - 1n) is accepted and not flagged.
rules.message: Arc's public RPC rejects eth_getLogs ranges over 10,000 blocks (-32012); a fixed start block to latest breaks as the chain grows (~2 blocks/s).
rules.fix: Page history in chunks of at most 9,999 blocks (step 9_999n, toBlock = fromBlock + 9_998n). Retry -32014 (that backend has not imported the block yet) after a short backoff.

span.message: Block range over 10,000 blocks (toBlock - fromBlock of 10,000 or more): Arc's public RPC rejects it with -32012.

evidence.quote: Reduce the range to ≤9,999 blocks per request and page through history sequentially

notes: The ERC-8004 tutorial (https://docs.arc.io/arc/tutorials/register-your-first-ai-agent) queries latestBlock - 10000n to latestBlock, which is 10,001 blocks; this rule flags that pattern.

Boundary checked live on 2026-10-04 (rpc.testnet.arc.network and rpc.testnet.arc.io): toBlock - fromBlock = 9,999 (10,000 blocks) returned a result, 10,000 (10,001 blocks) returned -32012 'requested range too large'. The rule flags only what the RPC rejects (the docs: 'exceeds 10,000 blocks'); the fix keeps the docs' 9,999-block advice.
-32014: the primary endpoint is load-balanced, and the backend serving a request may not have imported a block near the head yet (rpc-endpoints, Troubleshooting). It is not a rate limit.

Observed, not documented: a page within the block limit can still fail with -32602 'query exceeds max results N, retry with the range A-B' when it would return too many logs (N was 20,000 on both public endpoints on 2026-10-04). Split the page; the error names a sub-range that fits.

rules.title: Transfer log filter without the USDC system emitter
rules.flags: A Transfer filter (topic 0xddf252ad…, `event Transfer(`, eventName 'Transfer', filters.Transfer) with no `address` (error), both USDC emitters (error; also through a loop or .map over a const array that holds both), only the ERC-20 USDC address 0x3600… (warn), or 0x3600… and the system emitter in separate filters of one file (warn). Addresses are judged by value when the guard can resolve them. A spread ethers filter ({ ...token.filters.Transfer(…) }) is judged by its contract.
rules.message: Transfer filter with no emitter address: an ERC-20 USDC transfer logs twice (0x3600… at 6 decimals, system emitter at 18), so totals double and decimals mix.
rules.fix: Set address to the system emitter 0xffffFFFfFFffffffffffffffFfFFFfffFFFfFFfE alone (18 decimals): it logs every USDC movement, ERC-20 transfers included. Do not add 0x3600….

usdc-only.message: Filter on the ERC-20 USDC address (0x3600…) only: plain native USDC sends are missed. The system emitter logs every USDC movement, ERC-20 transfers included.
usdc-only.fix: Replace 0x3600… with the system emitter 0xffffFFFfFFffffffffffffffFfFFFfffFFFfFFfE (18 decimals). Do not query both: each ERC-20 transfer would come back twice.

evidence.quote: The native system emitter logs a `Transfer` for every explicit USDC transfer—native sends, ERC-20 transfers, mints, and burns—at 18-decimal precision.

both-emitters.message: Filter on both USDC emitters: each ERC-20 transfer returns two logs with different decimals (6 and 18), so totals double.
both-emitters.fix: Drop 0x3600… and query only the system emitter 0xffffFFFfFFffffffffffffffFfFFFfffFFFfFFfE (18 decimals); it already logs every ERC-20 transfer.

split-emitters.message: Transfer filters in this file read both USDC emitters in separate queries: each ERC-20 transfer is in both results, so merging them counts it twice.
split-emitters.fix: Read USDC movements from the system emitter 0xffffFFFfFFffffffffffffffFfFFFfffFFFfFFfE only (18 decimals). If you keep the 0x3600… query, never add its 6-decimal values to them.

evidence.quote: Match on the emitter address so you do not count the same movement twice, and never mix the 6-decimal and 18-decimal values.

rules.title: CCTP burn to Stellar (domain 27) without CctpForwarder
rules.flags: A burn to domain 27 (destinationDomain 27 or a Stellar domain constant; depositForBurn(…, 27, …) in ethers or viem write([…]) form) whose mintRecipient or destinationCaller is not CctpForwarder, or is zero, or a file that never references CctpForwarder or its contract ids.
rules.message: CCTP burn to domain 27 (Stellar) without CctpForwarder: unless mintRecipient and destinationCaller are both CctpForwarder, the USDC is stuck and cannot be recovered.
rules.fix: Set mintRecipient and destinationCaller to CctpForwarder (mainnet CBZL2IH7…DF5T, testnet CA66Q2WF…4VSZ) and pass the recipient strkey as forwardRecipient in hook data.

zero-caller.message: Burn to Stellar with a zero destinationCaller: CctpForwarder cannot complete the transfer and the USDC is stuck.

recipient-not-forwarder.message: Burn to Stellar whose mintRecipient or destinationCaller is not CctpForwarder: the USDC never reaches the recipient and cannot be recovered.

evidence.quote: On the source burn, both `mintRecipient` and `destinationCaller` must be set to the `CctpForwarder`

rules.title: Upstream Foundry instead of Arc Foundry
rules.flags: foundryup, foundry.paradigm.xyz, foundry-rs/foundry-toolchain, bare `forge create|test|script`, `anvil`, `cast send`; and `arc-forge test|script` or `arc-anvil` with no Arc mode (no --network arc, no FOUNDRY_PROFILE whose foundry.toml profile sets network = "arc", no --fork-url/--rpc-url), in scripts, Makefiles, package.json, README code blocks and CI (error in CI workflows).
rules.message: Upstream Foundry (foundryup, forge, anvil, cast, foundry-toolchain) is not Arc-aware: local simulation runs a standard EVM, so tests can pass and still fail on Arc.
rules.fix: Install Arc Foundry from its releases page and use arc-forge test --network arc, arc-anvil --network arc and arc-cast send.

ci.message: CI installs or runs upstream Foundry: a green run there does not cover Arc behavior.

arc-mode-off.message: arc-forge test/script or arc-anvil without Arc mode runs Ethereum rules locally, so tests can pass and still fail on Arc.
arc-mode-off.fix: Add --network arc, or use FOUNDRY_PROFILE=arc with [profile.arc] network = "arc" in foundry.toml, or fork an Arc RPC (--fork-url).

arc-mode-off-ci.message: CI runs arc-forge/arc-anvil without Arc mode, so it tests Ethereum rules: a green run there does not cover Arc behavior.
arc-mode-off-ci.fix: Add --network arc, or use FOUNDRY_PROFILE=arc with [profile.arc] network = "arc" in foundry.toml, or fork an Arc RPC (--fork-url).

evidence.quote: Tools that locally simulate the EVM (such as Foundry's `anvil`) run a standard EVM, not Arc's, and can't reproduce Arc-specific behavior.

notes: docs.arc.io uses the per-command flag (arc-forge test --network arc); the circlefin/arc-foundry README also documents a profile, [profile.arc] network = "arc" selected with FOUNDRY_PROFILE=arc (https://github.com/circlefin/arc-foundry#point-a-project-at-arc, checked 2026-10-04). Either form is accepted.

The same README shows that Arc Foundry without Arc mode runs Ethereum rules: "arc-forge test  # Ethereum" next to "FOUNDRY_PROFILE=arc arc-forge test  # Arc", and "Forking needs no Arc-specific configuration" because the chain ID is recognised (https://github.com/circlefin/arc-foundry#point-a-project-at-arc, checked 2026-10-04). The arc-mode-off variants rest on that README, not on docs.arc.io.
Circle's use-arc skill (circlefin/skills@58ab864) installs upstream Foundry with foundryup; where it conflicts with docs.arc.io, follow this rule.

rules.title: Memo or Multicall3From called from a smart account or contract
rules.flags: Memo 0x5294…e505 or Multicall3From 0x522f…47D0 in the same file as sendUserOperation, toCircleSmartAccount, toSafeSmartAccount, a bundler client or Safe; or a non-test Solidity contract calling memo / aggregate3 on them.
rules.message: Memo (0x5294…e505) and Multicall3From (0x522f…47D0) accept only a direct EOA caller; calls via a smart account, Safe, bundler or another contract revert.
rules.fix: Send Memo.memo / Multicall3From.aggregate3 as a plain EOA transaction (eth_sendTransaction); with a smart account, send the memo from an EOA or keep the metadata off-chain.

contract-caller.message: A contract calls Memo or Multicall3From: CallFrom rejects an intermediary msg.sender, so the call reverts.

evidence.quote: Smart contract wallets aren't supported as the direct caller.

notes: UNVERIFIED: behavior for EIP-7702-delegated EOAs and for wallet_sendCalls batches is not documented; the payouts starter avoids both.

rules.title: Value forwarding through Multicall3From
rules.flags: aggregate3Value or Call3Value in a file that uses Multicall3From, or a non-zero `value` on an aggregate3 call to Multicall3From.
rules.message: Multicall3From supports no value forwarding: there is no aggregate3Value, and CallFrom does not forward native value on Arc.
rules.fix: Call aggregate3 with no value and move USDC with ERC-20 transfer subcalls (6 decimals).

evidence.quote: `aggregate3Value` because `CallFrom` does not forward value on Arc.
